absent: Numeric encodings, bit positions, widths and safe value resolution rules for registers and fields.
Full struct layouts, sizes, offsets, alignment and lifetime for cpu info, feature descriptors and vector info.
Locking, concurrency and memory ordering rules for feature table and vector map updates.
Boot and secondary bring up ordering, capability finalisation timing and preemption context guarantees.
Vector quantum to byte length conversion and numeric minimum and maximum values.
Override provisioning, user mask policy and taint handling beyond the single out of specification signal.
Device tree binding details, sysfs permissions and fallback mask selection policy.

findings.text: Boot initialisation sorts the feature tables once then seeds sanitised views for cache, counter and AArch64 debug, instruction, memory, processor and vector extension families, handling 32 bit state, vector length maps, partitioning monitor and tag storage identifiers only when presence checks indicate them.

Secondary CPU onboarding merges each local identifier into the system view with per field safe resolution, re probes vector lengths while capabilities remain open, conditionally checks partitioning and tag identifiers, lazily adopts 32 bit state when permitted, then taints once if any strict view diverged.

Direct register read by encoding serves the full AArch32 and AArch64 identifier set plus cache and timer registers, applies configured override mask and value when a descriptor exists, and treats any other encoding as a fatal programming error.

Vector length management keeps per vector type a map of universally available quanta and a map of quanta seen anywhere; initialisation probes the boot CPU and duplicates the outcome, while later updates intersect the common map and union the partial map with each fresh probe.

Tag storage accessibility test returns negative unless memory tagging support is compiled in, otherwise locates the tagging field descriptor and evaluates the effective level with boot override interaction against the second generation threshold.

Capability predicates share an inclusive range matcher that extracts a scoped value and configured bounds with signedness awareness; variants accept always, test raw membership, or additionally require user visibility masking derived from the register user mask.
Task placement helper derives a fallback mask from task possibility combined with housekeeping domain CPUs for use when asymmetric feature support constrains placement.

Early boot parameters govern pseudo interrupt enablement and mismatched 32 bit userspace allowance, while a late init hook exposes the 32 bit capable mask through sysfs only when mismatch is permitted and a cpu subsystem root exists.

Pseudo interrupt support remains disabled unless explicitly enabled early, and is revoked during system detection when firmware attached to the interrupt controller advertises a broken save restore quirk; one build provides an empty detection alternative.
Scoped capability reads use the sanitised system view for system scope and a direct encoding read for local scope, and forbid local scope evaluation in a preemptible context.

System view updates leave identical fields untouched and resolve each differing field to a safe value rather than last writer wins, while strict mismatch detection compares only masked bits and reports register name with boot and secondary values before signalling taint.

Strictness can be relaxed per field by clearing mask bits with a warning on unknown fields; when mismatched 32 bit operation is allowed and boot lacked 32 bit support, the first secondary 32 bit snapshot becomes the boot baseline exactly once.
When the sanitised view shows no AArch32 at privileged level, privileged dependent security and virtualisation related fields are removed from strict checking to avoid spurious diagnostics.

32 bit userspace capability tolerates absence when mismatch is allowed and reports once at system scope when present; interrupt interface capability additionally requires higher level enablement; cache behaviour capabilities inspect coherence bits from system or local cache type views.

Divergent cache, zero block, counter, debug, instruction, memory, processor, vector, partitioning or tag views risk incorrect just in time code, wrong zero length on migration, broken timekeeping and virtualisation, debug inconsistency or unsafe tag handling, hence any strict divergence taints as out of specification.

When raw cache type hides data cache coherence that effective values show, the kernel adjusts the privileged control register to trap userspace cache type reads on that CPU so the safe effective value can be emulated.

Length probing begins at the architectural maximum quantum and moves downward, programming each candidate, reading back the effective length, stopping when the effective length exceeds the candidate, otherwise collapsing to the effective quantum and recording it before continuing.

Per CPU information holds separate 64 bit snapshots for cache, counter and each identifier family plus partitioning and tag values, and nests a 32 bit block holding debug, instruction, memory, processor and vector snapshots.

Feature handling uses per register descriptors carrying field rules, current system value, strict mask, name and override state, plus per field position and width and per capability register reference, position, width, signedness and inclusive bounds.

Managed AArch32 identifiers span two debug, seven instruction, six memory model, three processor feature and three media vector registers; managed AArch64 identifiers span cache type, zero block, counter frequency, two debug, four instruction, five memory, three processor and one each for scalable vector, matrix and floating extensions, with partitioning and tag identifiers handled only when presence indicates them.
Vector length handling defines an inclusive quantum interval with minimum and maximum bounds shared by both vector types, with bitmap sizing derived from the maximum.
